activity_title: Finish and prove the responsive rebuild at ten viewports
activity_summary: The scratchpad had been wiped overnight, so the before-baseline was rebuilt from git HEAD and confirmed byte-identical (md5 b1529309...). Measured both builds at 1920, 1600, 1440, 1366, 1280, 1024, 900, 768, 600 and 375: zero control overlaps, zero clipped labels, zero page-level horizontal overflow, header/body column drift 0.0px and zero console errors. A 25-state interaction harness plus an identical CSV hash proved nothing functional changed.
evidence_refs: markup+script+payload md5 identical before/after; 25 interaction states identical; CSV hash e6dada83
reusable_pattern: Rebuild a lost baseline from git rather than trusting a remembered number
validation_rule: A CSS-only change must leave every byte outside the style block untouched

activity_title: Hide the summary cards and Record ID, add the SOT column and the Category filter
activity_summary: Cards and the Record ID column are hidden by CSS only, so the KPI maths, the numbering and the CSV are untouched. SOT is a Yes/No badge from configurator.components_sot_skus matched on the SKU itself, never a prefix. Category is a longest-prefix rule; the two overlapping prefixes were settled from the SOT sheet's own source_tab - PH is 398 of 399 pendantholder and WS is 180 of 180 wallarm - so PH is Pendant Lamp Holder and WS is Wall Arm, not Lighting.
evidence_refs: SOT flags re-checked against the table: 0 mismatches; Wall Arm filter returns 34 of 34 WS SKUs
reusable_pattern: Resolve an ambiguous classification from the data's own reference table, never from the SKU prefix alone
validation_rule: Every derived flag re-verified against its source table after the build
next_action: Ask whether more SKUs should be added to the SOT sheet

activity_title: Cross-check every dashboard combo against the database
activity_summary: Derived all component-to-combo links for the in-scope components and compared them with what the dashboard showed: 391 database links versus 374 displayed, 0 extra. 13 of the 17 missing links were combos genuinely flagged deleted in the old database (verified as a live mirror, not a stale copy: identical row count and latest timestamps), and 4 were combos created after that build, which the rebuild picked up.
evidence_refs: 391 links vs 374 shown; after rebuild 378, only the 13 deleted missing; combos 301 -> 305

activity_title: Compact the filter bar to a maximum of two rows and one row on wide screens
activity_summary: Above 1024px the bar was flex, so each select sized itself to its longest option (Supplier 261px, Container 182px) and could never shrink, wrapping into 3-4 rows; below 1024px an auto-fill grid of equal 150px columns did the same. Replaced with a fixed grid - one row at 1560px and above, two rows from 768 to 1559px - with real size steps per breakpoint and a compacted header. Screenshots at the user's own width showed Search and Clear each taking a whole row before the fix.
evidence_refs: 1024px 223px/3 rows -> 117px/2 rows; 768px 275px/4 rows -> 108px/2 rows; 1920px 162px/2 rows -> 75px/1 row
reusable_pattern: Cap a select's width in a grid track; min-width alone never stops a select sizing to its longest option
validation_rule: Filter rows must stay at most 2 for every width from 768 to 1559px
gap_or_risk: Below 768px stacking is allowed for usability

activity_title: Rebuild the supply chain on the new old-supply tables and delete the history parsing
activity_summary: The three tables added by the user (old_supplyorder 987, old_supplyorderlist 15,635, old_supplier 120) became the fallback behind the new PO system. Resolution keeps the container that actually arrived: an arrived PO or a completed supply order, and when both exist the most recent arrival wins - proved necessary by IMACCW, whose Feb supply receipt is newer than its Dec PO. The status column holds both Completed (811) and completed (48), so lower(trim()) is mandatory. The supplier-PO INNER JOIN was removed from the scope and all free-text product_history parsing was deleted. An Incoming button was added for containers still on order or shipping.
evidence_refs: 311 completed components (68 PO + 243 supply); container 311/311; received 309/311; incoming 152
reusable_pattern: When two systems both claim an arrival, display the most recent one rather than preferring a system
validation_rule: grep for product_history and Supply - must return comments only
gap_or_risk: Deleted products excluded, so incoming is 152 not the user's 155
next_action: None - difference explained by the 3 deleted SKUs

activity_title: Audit the whole combo population and prove where combos were lost
activity_summary: Counted every population independently: 38,078 combo products exist, 3,446 created this year, but only 615 of them actually use a component created this year. The old database still holds the real structured table public.inv_product_combo (122,237 rows) and the LEDSone sku_original derivation reproduces it exactly - 781 shared links, 19 newer, 0 missed. The funnel showed the loss: 800 links, 786 after deleted combos, then 464 because discovery ran off the 311 completed components instead of the 677 base set. Also audited the 266 components with no supply record: only 4 are matching problems (trailing spaces or a typo), 157 hold stock with no record at all and 109 were simply never ordered.
evidence_refs: 800 links / 623 combos -> 786 / 615 -> 464 / 411; 204 hidden; 69 mixed; 266 no-supply split 4/157/109
reusable_pattern: Audit a population by defining it independently first, then funnelling stage by stage with a named drop reason
validation_rule: Every stage prints before, after, dropped and the reason
gap_or_risk: The 3,000+ expectation refers to all combos created this year, a different population
next_action: Give the database team the 4 typo SKUs and the 157 stock-without-record list

activity_title: Separate combo discovery from container status and ship the All Data mode
activity_summary: Combo discovery now runs from the 677-component base set instead of the 311 completed subset, and the combo-created-this-year condition was removed because the requirement constrains the component's creation date, restoring 17 combos and 29 relationships. Status became an attribute (COMPLETED 311, INCOMING 100, NO SUPPLY DATA 266) instead of a filter, and the Incoming button became All Data: default OFF keeps the completed-only view exactly, ON shows 677 components and 615 combos. A combo appears once however many qualifying components it has, and a completed component always supplies its container data.
evidence_refs: All Data 677 components / 885 rows and 615 combos / 1,201 rows; OFF restores 311 / 411; 0 duplicates; 0 deleted leakage; 0 console errors
reusable_pattern: Keep a second data mode as its own dataset behind a marked block, so deleting it restores the default view untouched
validation_rule: A combo appears once regardless of how many qualifying components it has
gap_or_risk: 266 components still have no PO and no supply record
next_action: Confirm whether the Components tab should also follow the base set
